title: Baked Rice Pudding
subtitle: Slow-baked creamy rice pudding
excerpt: Arborio rice baked slowly in a mixture of milk and cream with honey and nutmeg until thick and creamy. It needs very little attention and fills the kitchen with a gentle warmth as it cooks.
sourceNotes: Based on the traditional British baked rice pudding method using a slow oven and a mix of full-fat milk and cream.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days. Reheat with a splash of milk stirred in over low heat.
recipe.temperatureNote: 130C fan. A low oven is essential for creamy results.

content.text: Do not stir the pudding during cooking once the skin starts to form. The skin is the best part and breaking it early prevents it from setting properly.
Put the rice in a deep roasting tin or ovenproof dish.
Warm the milk and cream together in a saucepan until just steaming. Stir in the honey.
Pour the warm milk mixture over the rice. Stir once to distribute.
Grate the nutmeg over the top.
Bake for 2 hours, stirring once after the first 30 minutes. The pudding should be thick and golden on top.
Leave to stand for 5 minutes before serving. It will thicken further as it cools.

items.symptom: Pudding is still very liquid after 2 hours.
items.cause: Oven temperature too low or dish too wide.
items.fix: Increase to 160C and bake for a further 30 minutes.

items.cause: Not enough liquid or oven too low.
items.fix: Add 100ml more milk and continue baking.

items.cause: Oven not hot enough to form a proper skin.
items.fix: Grill for 2 minutes at the end to colour the top.
